## Requirement

Build a standalone Enterprise + Renewal Opportunity sales process for Northwind (12 reps, 2 managers, 1 sales-ops admin): two Sales Processes with staged probabilities and Path checklists, opportunity products against the Standard Price Book with a before-Propose product gate and a 20% discount cap enforced by validation rules, a formal manager approval process with record lock for over-cap discounts, a small record-page LWC (discount, approval status, Submit for approval) backed by an Apex invocable action, an open-pipeline report and a close-month dashboard tile, and two record types — all without touching the existing SMB process, and with no integration or data migration in scope.

## Scope

### In scope

- Two Opportunity sales processes for the Enterprise team - Enterprise (Qualify, Discover, Propose, Negotiate, Closed Won, Closed Lost) and Renewal (Renewal Review, Renewal Proposed, Closed Won, Closed Lost) - each with the probabilities and forecast buckets the requester signed off (requirement.md item 1; Q5, Q6, Q21, Q36).
- Two Opportunity record types (Enterprise, Renewal) bound to those two Sales Processes, plus the eight stage values they need added to the OpportunityStage standard value set (requirement.md item 1; Q8, Q36, Q40).
- Two header fields on Opportunity: Discount__c (Percent) typed by the rep, and Approval_Status__c (restricted picklist Pending/Approved/Rejected) written only by the approval process (requirement.md items 2-4; Q12, Q22).
- One page layout per new record type carrying the platform-required standard fields, Discount__c and Approval_Status__c (requirement.md item 4; Q14, Q20).
- A Path per record type with per-stage key fields and the exit checklist wording the requester dictated (requirement.md item 1; Q2, Q11, Q46, Q48, Q49).
- A validation rule blocking Closed Won above a 20% discount unless the approval is Approved, with a Custom Permission bypass granted by permission set to the sales-ops admin only (requirement.md item 2; Q13, Q15, Q17).
- A validation rule requiring at least one product line before Propose - planned, and BLOCKED on a library coverage gap rather than guessed (requirement.md item 2; Q11, Q42).
- A declarative Approval Process on Opportunity: entry above a 20% discount, approver = the rep's manager through the user hierarchy, record locked while pending with AdminOnly editability, recall allowed, and the four action sets the requester specified (requirement.md item 3; Q27, Q28, Q31, Q32, Q33, Q58, Q59, Q60, Q61).
- Three Classic email templates in a public folder plus the two workflow alerts and four field updates the approval process fires (requirement.md item 3; Q33).
- An Apex service, an @AuraEnabled controller and an @InvocableMethod action that submit exactly one Opportunity into that process, with the test class the requester asked for (requirement.md item 4; Q29, Q30, Q34, Q35).
- A record-page LWC showing the discount and the approval status with a Submit-for-approval button enabled only when the rule requires it, plus its Jest suite (requirement.md item 4; Q22, Q34, Q35, Q51, Q52).
- A Lightning record page carrying the Path and that component, with the org-default record-page assignment (requirement.md item 4; Q50).
- A custom report type, a summary report of open Enterprise pipeline by stage with amount and discount, a pipeline-by-close-month dashboard, and the two folders shared to the Enterprise Managers public group (requirement.md item 5; Q23, Q24, Q25, Q54, Q55, Q56, Q57, Q63).
- A configuration workbook, traceability matrix, acceptance criteria, UAT case pack, build-level package.xml and a go-live runbook covering the 140-deal record-type reassignment, folder sharing, approval process order and the record-page activation (Q8, Q25, Q26).

### Out of scope

- Any change to the SMB generic sales process, its record type, its two list views or its pipeline report - explicitly descoped by Q4 and Q9; the build adds stage values and record types beside it and touches none of its metadata.
- Any sharing change: no org-wide default change, no sharing rule, no role-hierarchy edit. Q4 answered that the separation is process guidance only and Q24 answered that manager visibility already comes from the role hierarchy.
- Opportunity splits, opportunity teams and the Private flag - Q7 answered no to all three.
- Any integration, inbound or outbound - requirement.md item 6, confirmed by Q38 and Q65.
- Any data migration. The 140 open Enterprise deals are reassigned by the sales-ops admin as a post-go-live runbook step, not by a build step - Q8.
- Cleaning up the ~20 open Enterprise deals with no products and the 6 with discounts above 20%: Q16 answered that the rules apply on the next save only and no clean-up is in scope.
- Creating Product2, Pricebook2 or PricebookEntry records. requirement.md states the org already has Sales Cloud Enterprise, Product2 and a Standard Price Book; this build uses the catalogue rather than building it.
- Notifying Finance or Customer Success when a deal closes - Q3 answered that both read the record and the report covers it, with no notification build in scope.
- Subscriptions, scheduled emails and exports of the report or dashboard - Q53 was informational and was left unanswered with no documented default, so nothing is built for it (assumption A30).
- Creating the Enterprise Managers public group membership. Group metadata carries no members (admin/queues-and-public-groups); the group ships empty and the sales-ops admin adds the two managers and the VP in Setup (assumption A32).
- Historical trending of the Enterprise pipeline (a reporting snapshot): Q56 was informational and left unanswered at G1, the current-snapshot default is applied per assumption A42, and trending would need its own step and a forward-only data start - so it is named here rather than absorbed silently into the dashboard step.

## Decisions

| Id | Decision | Decision tree | Branch | ADR | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `D1` | Add the six Enterprise stages and the two Renewal-only stages to the OpportunityStage StandardValueSet as a full merge of the org's currently active values, not as a partial file listing only the new ones. | — | — | ✔ | automation-selection.md, flow-pattern-selector.md and sharing-selection.md were each read end to end; none of them routes a picklist-value deploy, and standards/decision-trees/README.md lists no tree that does. The skill reference is the source: section 3 states that the deactivate-by-omission rule of api_meta.txt:47482-47483 applies to StandardValueSet too, 'so a partial file is a mass deactivation'. That single sentence is what turns an obvious-looking file into a decision. |
| `D2` | Two Sales Processes bound to two Record Types, rather than one wide process exposing all ten stages to both motions. | — | — | ✔ | No decision tree routes between one process and many; the trade is documented in the skill, which names the single-catch-all process as anti-pattern 1 - it 'forces every record type to expose all stages, including irrelevant ones for that motion' and makes forecast rollups unreliable. Q36's default said the same. The Path constraint settles what was left: only one PathAssistant may exist per record type per object, so two guidance sets require two record types whatever the stage lists did. |
| `D3` | Enforce the 20% discount cap with a Validation Rule carrying a $Permission bypass, not with a record-triggered Flow or Apex. | — | — | ✔ | automation-selection.md was read end to end and the requirements-clarifier had already filed the same finding: the tree's scope is six automation engines and Validation Rule is not one of them, so its Q-tree has no branch that reaches this choice and citing Q2 or Q3 would be a fabricated ground. The skill reference carries it instead: its Example 1 is a discount-shaped Opportunity rule with the bypass clause first inside the AND, which is the exact shape M2-S03 ships. |
| `D4` | Manager sign-off is a declarative Approval Process with a record lock and an approval history, not a Flow approval or a custom Apex approval object. | — | — | ✔ | automation-selection.md's numbered tree does not reach Approval Process at all - Q1's trigger list has no option for 'a business decision needing one person's sign-off' - and its only mention is an unnumbered cheat-sheet row, 'Approval chain \| Approval Process -> Flow post-approval \| Flow with branching \| Apex custom approval'. A row is not a branch, so no branch id is cited and the skill carries the decision. Q3's requirement clauses - outcome and comments on the record, locked while pending - are what the native engine gives and a Flow would have to re-implement. |
| `D5` | The Submit-for-approval control is an LWC calling imperative Apex, not a Screen Flow quick action. | `standards/decision-trees/automation-selection.md` | Q8 |  | Q1's 'a user clicking a button or filling a form' reaches Q7; Q7's 'Yes (record page)' reaches Q8. Q8's condition is a conjunction - under 10s AND without custom UI - and requirement.md item 4 asks for custom UI in so many words: a component that shows the discount and the approval status alongside a button whose enabled state is a rule. The submit itself would finish well inside 10s, so it is the custom-UI half that makes the answer No, and the No leaf names the component and the template it should be built from. |
| `D6` | The LWC entry point (@AuraEnabled) and the Flow-invocable action (@InvocableMethod) are separate classes over one service class, rather than one class carrying both annotations. | — | — | ✔ | Q34's answer calls for an invocable Apex action, and an LWC can only import an @AuraEnabled method - so the obvious shape is one method carrying both. The gotcha forbids it in the guide's own words: 'The only annotation that can be used with the InvocableMethod annotation is Deprecated' (apexdev L5430), and 'Only one method in a class can have the InvocableMethod annotation' (L5422), with the remedy stated as 'One action per outer class; share the body through a service.' No decision tree routes an annotation choice. |
| `D7` | Manager visibility of their own reps' Enterprise pipeline is left to the existing role hierarchy: no org-wide default change, no sharing rule, no Apex managed sharing. | `standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md` | Q2 |  | Q24's answer states the mechanism outright - 'Each manager sees only their own reps' pipeline on the report (role hierarchy does that)' - and Q4 ruled out any sharing change. Reading the tree from START with U = an Enterprise manager and the record owner = one of their reps, Q2's first leaf is the terminal answer: the manager is above the owner in the hierarchy and hierarchy access is on, so the access already exists and no later layer is needed. Q1 was read first and is not the branch that resolves this - it only routes on the current OWD, which this build does not change. |
| `D8` | The approval process's entry criteria is a formula (Discount__c > 0.20), not a criteriaItems row comparing to 20. | — | — | ✔ | A Percent field carries the fraction in formula context and the plain number outside it: 'percent fields are expressed divided by 100 in formulas (100% is expressed as 1; 50% is expressed as 0.5)', and the same gotcha spells out that a Decision comparing the field directly is on the other path and must be bounded with > 50 rather than > 0.5. Only the formula half is grounded in this library. entryCriteria takes criteriaItems OR formula and never both, so choosing the formula puts the threshold in the one representation the corpus settles - and makes it identical to the validation rule's, which is what a reader of both files will expect. |
| `D9` | The approval process ships active true, overriding the deploy-inactive guidance its own skill gives for a production deploy. | — | — | ✔ | Grounded on the two places in this library that state the Active requirement itself. admin/approval-process-apex-patterns/references/metadata-examples.md lines 49-53: '<active>true</active> - required field. The ProcessDefinition preflight query below asserts State = Active; an inactive process is invisible to a submission that names it.' And the same skill's templates/approval-process-apex-patterns-template.md line 30, the preflight row: 'Is the process State = Active? \| \| A named submission to an inactive process fails'. M3-S03's Apex passes the bare developer name Discount_Approval to setProcessDefinitionNameOrId, so what this build ships is exactly the named submission both lines describe. The deploy-inactive guidance in the same file at lines 515-517 - 'A production process should deploy inactive and be activated after its workflow actions and templates exist' - is written for a SPLIT deploy; this build ships the two workflow alerts, the four field updates, the three email templates and the process in one package, so the condition that guidance waits for is already met at deploy time. Overriding published production guidance is still an accepted risk rather than a neutral choice: assumption A36 records it and it carries the process-order prerequisite A34. Correction to plan v1, which cited gotcha 14 for this: that citation was wrong. Gotcha 14's subject is a NULL processDefinitionNameOrId routing by org process order, which is the opposite case, and it says nothing about a named process requiring State Active. The citation is replaced here rather than the conclusion re-argued. |
| `D10` | The record page's org-default assignment ships as actionOverrides on objects/Opportunity/Opportunity.object-meta.xml inside the same step as the FlexiPage, rather than on the object-model step. | — | — | ✔ | A FlexiPage carries no assignment of its own; the org default lives in an actionOverrides block on the object file, one per formFactor. check_lightning_record_page_configuration.py reads object files with objects/*/*.object-meta.xml relative to --manifest-dir and does not recurse, so the override and the page have to sit in one step directory or the assignment check cannot run at all. Run against this plan's M3-S05 fixture it went from four ERRORs and exit 1 to 'No errors found' and exit 0 once the override and the three component identifiers were added. |

- `D1`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/picklist-and-value-sets/references/metadata-examples.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Ship only the eight new values and let the platform merge them; Create the stages in Setup by hand and deploy nothing; Use a GlobalValueSet instead of the standard value set
  - Consequences: The build cannot produce the deployable file offline: the union needs the org's current list. M1-S01's deploy-order.md leads with the retrieve, assumption A24 carries the risk at high, and the M1 gate has a manual tick on the diff.
- `D2`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/opportunity-management/references/well-architected.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: One Sales Process with all ten stages; Two processes on one record type; A picklist filter instead of a BusinessProcess
  - Consequences: Two record types means two layouts, two Paths, two recordTypeVisibilities rows and a layout assignment that only a Profile can carry - which is why M2-S02 exists and why it is human-gated.
- `D3`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/validation-rules/references/metadata-examples.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Before-save record-triggered Flow raising a fault; Apex before-update trigger; Layout-level Required on Discount__c
  - Consequences: The rule fires on every save path including the API, which Q42's default asked for. It also means the only escape is the Custom Permission, so the bypass permission set becomes a human-gated access step and every use has to be recorded by hand (Q17).
- `D4`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/approval-processes/SKILL.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Screen Flow approval with a custom status field; Apex custom approval records; Chatter approval post
  - Consequences: Record locking, approval history and the approver hierarchy come free, but process ORDER is not in the metadata and has to be set in Setup after deploy (assumption A34), and the rejection comments cannot be quoted in the email (assumption A27).
- `D5`
  - Branch quote: Q8. Can the action complete in under 10s without custom UI? ├── Yes → Screen Flow with Quick Action OR simple Headless Quick Action (Flow) └── No → LWC calling imperative Apex (see templates/lwc/patterns/imperativeApexPattern.js)
  - Alternatives rejected: Screen Flow with a Quick Action; Headless Quick Action (Flow); The standard Submit for Approval action on the layout
  - Consequences: An LWC and an Apex controller put this build under a 75% Apex coverage gate it would not otherwise have, which is why M3-S03 ships a test class and why M3-S04 ships a Jest suite.
- `D6`
  - Source reference: `skills/apex/invocable-methods/references/gotchas.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: One class with @AuraEnabled and @InvocableMethod on the same method; One class with both annotations on different methods; Drop the invocable and expose only @AuraEnabled
  - Consequences: Three classes plus a test rather than one. check_invocable_methods.py's IM001 is the regression guard - it was run against a deliberately broken copy of this step's own output and fired CRITICAL at exit 1, so the test on M3-S03 is known to be live rather than vacuous.
- `D7`
  - Branch quote: Q2. Is U in the same role or above the record owner's role in the hierarchy? ├── Yes, and "Grant access using hierarchies" is ON → Access already granted; done ├── Yes, but hierarchy is disabled on T → Q3 └── No → Q3
  - Alternatives rejected: Criteria-based sharing rule on RecordTypeId; Opportunity teams; Tightening the Opportunity OWD
  - Consequences: The dashboard is the one place this does not hold: Q24 asked for the full pipeline on the tile, so it runs as a SpecifiedUser and every viewer sees the VP's access level regardless of their own - which is why M4-S02 is human-gated and why assumption A29 exists.
- `D8`
  - Source reference: `skills/flow/flow-formula-and-expression-patterns/references/gotchas.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: criteriaItems on Opportunity.Discount__c greaterThan 20; criteriaItems greaterThan 0.20; A formula field holding the boolean
  - Consequences: The component's design attribute stays 20 because it reads the UI API rather than a formula, so the two representations coexist in one build. The Jest suite pins the component's reading, and assumption A35 makes the divergence a deploy-order check rather than a surprise.
- `D9`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/approval-process-apex-patterns/references/metadata-examples.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Ship active false and activate by hand; Ship active false and have the Apex omit setProcessDefinitionNameOrId; Ship two packages
  - Consequences: Process order still has to be set in Setup - the metadata carries no order - which is assumption A34 and a line in M3-S02's deploy-order.md. The Apex is unaffected either way because it names the process explicitly. Filed for the library and NOT for this build to resolve: admin/approval-process-apex-patterns contradicts itself on this point. Its prose at references/metadata-examples.md:515-517 says a production process should deploy inactive, while its own checker at scripts/check_approval_process_apex_patterns.py:376-386 raises HIGH on <active>false</active> whenever Apex in the same tree names the process - and cites gotcha 14 for a rule gotcha 14 does not state. No plan can satisfy both halves of one skill. This build follows the checker and the two sources above that do state the Active requirement, and records the disagreement as a library defect for the depth-wave worklist rather than resolving it in a build plan.
- `D10`
  - Source reference: `skills/admin/lightning-record-page-configuration/references/examples.md`
  - Alternatives rejected: Put actionOverrides on the object-model step; Assign the page by hand in Lightning App Builder; Assign it through an application file
  - Consequences: It bends build-planner Step 6 rule 6, which says object-level children belong to the object-model step. Nothing collides - M1-S01 writes the decomposed recordTypes, businessProcesses and fields files and no Opportunity.object-meta.xml at all - but the tension between that rule and a non-recursive checker is real and is filed as driver's-log material. An app with its own Opportunity record page still wins over the org default (assumption A38).

### M2 — Guidance, guardrails and who may bypass them

Goal: Given the M1 data model is accepted, when the M2 artefacts are deployed, then reps see a stage path carrying the exit criteria and key fields for each stage, an Enterprise or Renewal deal above a 20% discount cannot be set to Closed Won without an approved approval, the sales-ops admin is the only person who can save past that rule, and the 12 reps and 2 managers can select both new record types and get the right layout.

### M3 — The discount approval and the rep's panel

Goal: Given the guardrails are accepted, when the M3 artefacts are deployed, then a rep on an Enterprise or Renewal opportunity with a discount above 20% sees a panel showing the discount and the approval status with an enabled Submit button, submitting routes the request to their manager and locks the record, approving or rejecting writes the status back and emails the rep, recalling clears it, and all of it renders on one record page alongside the stage path.
